solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Description of characters from film but not stage

definitions.text: Description of characters from film but not stage

parts.words: Description of characters from film but not stage
parts.note: the letters F, I, L, M run in A-to-Z order, while S, T, A, G, E do not, so the word describing the first set and not the second is the one wanted

explanation.surface: Someone describes the cast of a movie as opposed to a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like actors in a film but means letters: the four letters of 'film' stand in dictionary order, the letters of 'stage' do not.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters arranged as they stand in the ABC are said to be in this kind of order.

clue.text: Intelligence agency backtracking about turning nasty and weak

indicators.note: about means the reversed agency letters go around the other piece
backtracking means the agency's letters read in reverse

parts.note: the CIA, the US Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: turning means the word for nasty is written backwards

parts.note: mean means nasty or unkind

explanation.surface: A spy agency retreats on turning nasty and weakens.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pale and lacking vigour, from too few red blood cells, makes someone feeble.

clue.text: Father of Apollo?

parts.note: Apollo was worshipped by Romans too, so his father would be addressed by the Latin word for father

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for father, still used jokingly in English, fits a father in a Roman-worshipped god's family.

clue.text: Opinion of cut bouquet with a china container

indicators.note: container means a and the word for friend hold the shortened praise

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so pal

indicators.note: cut means the word for compliment loses its last letter

parts.note: a bouquet is a compliment, or praise

explanation.surface: A view on a trimmed bunch of flowers placed in a china vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' and 'china' suggest flowers and porcelain; in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: An evaluation or assessment of something is a considered opinion of it.

clue.text: Language is abrupt losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the word for abrupt drops its first letter

parts.note: terse means curt or abrupt

explanation.surface: Someone's way of speaking turns curt when they lose their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland, a language.

clue.text: Lonely single proposed to go without love

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, single

indicators.note: to go without means the word for proposed goes outside the love letter

parts.note: slated means planned or proposed, as slated for next week
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A single person who proposed marriage must now live without love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut off and alone, someone set apart from others is lonely.

clue.text: Square described by Euclid?

parts.note: Euclid, a geometer, sounds like he describes squares, but as a Greek he would name a town square in his own tongue

explanation.definitionFit: This was the open public meeting place of an ancient Greek city, a square of the kind Euclid knew.

clue.text: State possibly embraces oddly laic faith

indicators.note: embraces means the region word holds the selected letters

parts.note: a region, for example a state, is an area

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of laic

explanation.surface: A state can take in secular folk and still have a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laic' means lay or secular, making the surface a paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of belief and worship is a faith.

clue.text: Light touch changing hot to cold

indicators.note: changing means one letter of the word for touch is swapped for another

parts.note: to handle something is to touch it
H for hot, as on a tap
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A light touch on a thermostat moves it from hot to cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax stick with a wick gives light, the oldest household lamp.

clue.text: Iberian tip as tomato covers tapas

indicators.note: the words around it cover the wanted run of letters, which sits across Iberian, tip, as and tomato

explanation.surface: A Spanish serving tip: put tomato on top of your bar snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'covers' as a topping; it signals letters concealed in 'IberiAN TIP AS TOmato'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are Mediterranean starters of small savoury bites; an Italian starter platter is a fair equivalent for Spanish bar nibbles.

clue.text: Plato, finally colossal Greek character

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the name Plato

parts.note: mega means huge or colossal

explanation.surface: A tribute to Plato as a towering figure of Greek thought.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet is a character in the sense of a written letter.

clue.text: Army doctor keeping cheerful in retreat

indicators.note: the doctor's letters keep, or hold, the other piece between them

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine

indicators.note: in retreat means the word for cheerful goes backwards

parts.note: airy means light-hearted and cheerful

explanation.surface: A military medic manages to stay upbeat while the troops fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' looks like an adjective for the doctor but is the definition in its sense of a vast crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An army can mean a huge number of anything, and a countless host is exactly that.

clue.text: Fruit having a dull all over skin

indicators.note: all over is read as turned over, so a and the word for dull go backwards

parts.note: mat (or matt) means dull, not glossy
rind is the skin of a fruit

explanation.surface: A fruit whose skin is dull right across its surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' is read as 'turned over', a reversal signal, not 'everywhere' as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical tree's pods hold a sour pulp used in cooking, so it is a fruit.

clue.text: Vulgar people who row in church

indicators.note: in places the rowers inside the church letters

parts.note: CE, the Church of England
oars can mean oarsmen, those who row

explanation.surface: Rowing crews who behave crudely at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but means rowing; OARS is an old name for oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude, rough or lacking refinement are all shades of vulgar.

clue.text: Means to get inscribed occasionally in Times

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the word for times

parts.note: ages are eras or times

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of inscribed, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A way to be written up occasionally in The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' picks the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of 'inscribed'; 'Times' is eras, not the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The agency of something is the means through which it acts, and plural channels are means.

clue.text: Turned in bulletin if editor's certain

indicators.note: Turned says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An editor is sure about something in a news bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters ETINIFED sit in 'bullETIN IF EDitor's'; 'Turned' reads them backwards. 'in' is the signal that they are concealed there.
explanation.definitionFit: Something definite is fixed and beyond doubt, which is what certain means.

clue.text: Dead foolish to stifle the setter's twisted cheers

indicators.note: to stifle means the word for foolish smothers the rest inside it

parts.note: inane means silly or foolish
the setter's is I am, written I'M

indicators.note: twisted means the word for cheers is turned round

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A setter makes a silly, muffled cheer about something dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the setter's' means 'the setter is', I'M. TA is everyday British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless things, like a stone, are without life just as the dead are.

clue.text: Bird with rising speed catches bat

indicators.note: catches means the outer letters capture the next piece
rising, in a down clue, means the word for speed reads upwards

parts.note: pace means speed
to bat a ball is to hit it

explanation.surface: A fast-flying bird catches a bat on the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bat' looks like the flying animal but means to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a folk name for birds with white crowns, such as the redstart, so a type of bird.

clue.text: Cunning shot bagging bird before opening of Twelfth

indicators.note: bagging means the shot's letters capture the others inside

parts.note: a shy is a throw or shot, as at a coconut shy

indicators.note: before puts the bird ahead of the next letter

parts.note: the teal is a small duck

indicators.note: opening of takes the first letter of Twelfth

explanation.surface: A sly marksman bags a bird at the start of the grouse season on the Glorious Twelfth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glorious Twelfth, 12 August, opens grouse shooting in Britain. A coconut shy is a fairground stall where you throw at targets.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy action is furtive and sly, which is what cunning describes here.

clue.text: Briny empty ocean covers fleet

indicators.note: covers, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second
empty means the word for ocean loses its inside letter

parts.note: the sea is the ocean
a shipping line is a fleet of ships

explanation.surface: A salty, deserted ocean surrounds a fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt solution is salty water, the same quality as briny.

clue.text: Goaded to employ new expletive

indicators.note: to employ means the dared letters take on, hold, the new letter

parts.note: dared means challenged or goaded into doing something

explanation.surface: Someone provoked into using a fresh swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild curse word, used as in 'that darned cat', is a kind of expletive.

clue.text: Outskirts of Dungeness skirting English Channel docks

indicators.note: skirting means those outer letters go around the next pieces
outskirts of takes the first and last letters of Dungeness

parts.note: a duct is a channel or tube

explanation.surface: A view of the Kent coast at Dungeness, near English Channel docks.
explanation.walkthrough: Dungeness is a headland on the Kent coast. 'English Channel' looks like the sea but splits into E and DUCT; 'docks' is a verb, takes off.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock wages is to take money off them, which is to subtract.

clue.text: Sex following diet's end of missionary position

indicators.note: following puts the word for sex after the diet word

parts.note: lo-cal, short for low-calorie, describes diet food
it is a coy term for sex or sex appeal

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of missionary

explanation.surface: A saucy line about sex and the missionary position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missionary position' looks like one phrase but splits: the last letter of 'missionary', then 'position' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A locality is a place or site, the place where something is situated.

clue.text: Hen party's finale in physical upset

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the overturned word
upset, in a down clue, means the word for physical is turned upside down

parts.note: real means physical, actual

indicators.note: finale takes the last letter of party

explanation.surface: At a hen party's climax, things get physical and someone is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a British bride's night out before her wedding; here 'Hen' is a laying bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen kept for its eggs is one that lays them.

clue.text: Low bone exposed dislodging middle of tibia

parts.note: a rib is a bone

indicators.note: dislodging means a letter is knocked out of the word for exposed

parts.note: bald means bare or exposed

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of tibia

explanation.surface: A grim injury report: a bone stuck out after the shin bone broke.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of 'tibia' is B, which leaves BALD as ALD.
explanation.definitionFit: Low humour that is coarse or bawdy is the sense of low here.

clue.text: Battle leaders of army lost against Mexico originally

indicators.note: leaders of takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A battle in which the army's commanders lost to Mexico at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the history: the Texan defenders lost this 1836 siege to Mexican forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1836 siege of a Texan mission by Mexican troops is a famous battle.

clue.text: Pubs supporters getting stood up inside

indicators.note: getting stood up inside means the middle pair of letters is turned upwards

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments

explanation.surface: Pub regulars who support the team are stood up by their dates.
explanation.walkthrough: In BRAS the inner RA is turned round to AR, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Places that serve drinks over a counter are bars, the same as pubs.

clue.text: Deprived one fed by skipping starters

indicators.note: skipping starters drops the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A hungry person fed by someone who skipped the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first letters of 'one', 'fed' and 'by' (O, F, B) to leave NE, ED, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The poor and deprived are those in want, lacking basic necessities.

clue.text: Risk is reduced taking horse and carriage

indicators.note: taking means the shortened word holds the horse inside it
is reduced means the word for risk loses its final letter

parts.note: a chance is a risk, as in taking a chance
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A cautious coachman lowers the risk by hitching up a horse and carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse and carriage' looks like one item; 'horse' is wordplay and 'carriage' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word for a motor coach on outings comes from a horse-drawn vehicle with benches, a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Foolish French writer almost accepts European bill

indicators.note: accepts means the shortened name takes the other pieces in
almost means the novelist's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Marcel Proust, French novelist
a bill is a poster, as in billposter

explanation.surface: A French novelist nearly agrees to a European proposal of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like a parliamentary bill but means a printed notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurd or utterly unreasonable is foolish to an extreme degree.
